Notes on sourdough hydration

Posted on 12 March 2026 by Sam

Hydration is the ratio of water to flour by weight. A dough made with 700 g of water and 1,000 g of flour is at 70% hydration.

Higher hydration gives a more open crumb, but the dough is harder to shape, and it needs stronger gluten development through folds.

For a first loaf, start at 65% and increase by five points once the shaping feels comfortable.
